(i) Deep learning is formulated, for the first time, as a discrete time control problem; (ii) A rigorous analysis of a training algorithm for deep learning is presented, which sheds light, for the first, time on its dynamics and means of stabilization; (iii) A principled method to train neural networks with ternary weights is presented, which yields competitive performance and interesting sparsity.
